newsitem.title: UK: UK's Energis offers 10p per minute US calls.
newsitem.headline: UK's Energis offers 10p per minute US calls.

text.p: Energis, the UK telecommunications company owned by the National Grid electricity transmission network, said on Monday it would offer business customers a record low 10p per minute call rate to the U.S.
From October 10, Energis' trans-Atlantic telephone rates will undercut telecom giant British Telecommunications' base rate by 50 percent, it added in a statement.
The company, which has been lobbying to be allowed to carry international calls in its own right, said it was also cutting charge for calls to Australasia, Japan and the Far East.

"The move places increasing pressure on other UK telecom operators and allows Energis to claim a minimum differential of 24 percent below BT base rate on daytime calls to these routes," the firm stated.

The company, whose 4,100 km of fibre optic cables are strung mainly across the National Grid's electricity pylons, said its business customers spent about 150 stg a month per site on international calls.

"The entry level has been set to ensure that large corporations and small to medium-sized businesses can benefit from direct dial costs to the U.S. at the lowest level ever," said chief executive Mike Grabiner.

Grabiner said the company, which began trading late in 1994 and whose customers include the BBC, British Gas, ICL, Virgin Atlantic Airways and Boots, intended to maintain efficiencies that allowed it to offer price advantages.
Energis, which supplies telephony services to 12,000 customers, made an operating loss of 72.8 million stg in the year to March 1996. It is expected to break even in 2000.

The National Grid said in June that it was in talks "with various people" about whether to sell a stake or link up with another company -- or companies -- to boost Energis's competitive position by adding an international dimension and improving local access.
